reviewEvidence: Review of revision-9745e692 (Phase 3 / Selection integrity) by an INDEPENDENT adversarial reviewer — a fresh-context agent with no memory of the implementation — briefed to falsify four specific claims rather than to summarise intent: (a) that a v1 session log restores exactly as before, (b) that a stale container ID can never be trusted, (c) that a failed or cancelled `use` never engages (and the converse: that a successful one cannot fail to engage), and (d) that an explicit selection can never be clobbered by auto-selection. It was also told to check every acceptance criterion against the code rather than the tests, to sweep the repository for stale consumers of the changed shapes, to run the security profile, and to attack the new JSONC scanner with hostile inputs. Its value was immediate: it falsified (a) at no cost but FOUND AND PROVED a regression of AC-4 that the author's own tests could not see, because those tests only ever called the reconciliation WITH a configuration hint. VERDICT: AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-5, AC-6, AC-7, AC-8 and AC-9 are satisfied as tested; AC-4 is NOT satisfied end-to-end, so this revision is blocked. The blocking finding and the majors/minors below are fixed in the working tree (commit 6ff66c3) and await the next sealed revision, where they will be re-verified. Clean per the independent pass: typecheck (no errors), 32 files / 381 tests at that revision, `dist` carrying the new code, v1-only logs restoring identically through the real reader path, no `--config` path smuggling (every candidate is validated by `resolveConfigCandidate`/`candidatesOf`), and the host-exec / stop / remove gates untouched. Also verified clean: every store write path is either membership-tested or the (now atomic) auto-select, which is the only unguarded writer.

findings.message: FIXED PENDING RE-SEAL. `reconcileSelection` was called without a configuration by the `up` handler and by the `list` repair, so `selectionFor` fell back to the workspace's discovered primary and `reconcileSelection` re-persisted that primary. The selected configuration therefore reverted — for the mapping, the prompt context and the host container-path guard, and across the reload — immediately after the `use` → `up` flow the extension itself tells the operator to run. Proven with a direct call against the built module: `reconcile(..., {workspaceKey})` returned `candidate.configPath = undefined` and persisted a record with no `configPath`, while the same call with the named path in the hint returned it. The AC-4 tests missed it because they only ever pass the hint. Fix (6ff66c3): the reconciliation carries the CURRENT selection's configuration whenever the caller provides none, per workspace, so an already-selected config is never dropped; an explicit hint still wins; nothing is carried across workspaces.

FIXED PENDING RE-SEAL. `/devcontainer off` held across a reload but not within the session: Pi cannot unregister the container tools, and `ExecutionService.exec` auto-selects whenever the store is empty, so the next `devcontainer_exec` resurrected the target the operator had just turned off — while README/CHANGELOG claimed the opt-out suppresses engagement until the operator selects again. Fix (6ff66c3): `allowsAutoSelection(decision)` gates the extension's auto-select hook on the session being engaged, and `off` records its true reason (`opted-out`) instead of `no-evidence`. The docs now also name the one exception (`activation: "always"` outranks the opt-out, deliberately: the operator's configuration says take over).

FIXED PENDING RE-SEAL. Parse failures were reported, but a READ failure (`EACCES`, a vanished file, a swapped symlink) still returned empty facts silently, leaving the host container-path guard inactive with nothing said — half of AC-1's "reported rather than looking like a config that declares no mapping". `readWorkspaceConfig` now reports read failures through the same diagnostic path. Related, recorded rather than changed: the sink is drained by the `/devcontainer` dispatch (that is the surface with a guaranteed UI), so a diagnostic raised by the per-turn context reaches the operator at the next `/devcontainer` command. The `Pi` hooks that could drain it per turn (`before_agent_start`, `tool_call`) receive no command context to notify with.

FIXED PENDING RE-SEAL. The JSONC scanner treated an unterminated block comment as a comment running to end-of-file, so `parseJsonc('{"a":1} /* oops')` returned a mapping from a document that was actually truncated — the same fail-open shape L0-02 is about, one layer down. It is now a syntax error, which the caller reports as `unparsable`. Everything else the reviewer threw at the scanner held: nested/escaped quotes, `\u` escapes, CRLF, a trailing comma with a comment between the comma and the bracket, a leading BOM; a lone `/` and empty input throw.

FIXED PENDING RE-SEAL. The AC-8 test enqueued the explicit selection first and therefore proved FIFO ordering rather than the production window (snapshot → awaited discovery → auto-select commit). A test now reproduces that ordering with a real await gap: the auto-selection is refused and the explicit selection survives. The design's matrix also cited `tests/unit/execution-service.test.ts` for this criterion, a file the branch never touched; the row now names the test that exists.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT — and now pinned. The reviewer warned that a failed `use` might still persist evidence that engages the session after a reload, contradicting AC-6's "leaves the session exactly as it was". Traced: the ambiguous and no-candidate paths return before `applySelection`, so nothing is persisted, and the test now asserts an empty persisted list for the ambiguous case. A restored-but-ambiguous record does activate on reload by design: it records a real earlier selection, and `bind()` still fails closed with the ambiguity remedy.

RECORDED. The converse of AC-6: a successful `up` whose refreshed registry does not know the workspace now leaves the session dormant (no engagement), where the old code engaged unconditionally. Engaging would be wrong — `bind()` would refuse — and the operator is not left guessing: the `up` result reports `selection: <status>`, which reaches them now that command output is actually delivered (Phase 2's fix). Kept as a note so a future change to the engagement gate does not have to rediscover the trade-off.

RECORDED. When a configuration declares no `workspaceFolder`/`workspaceMount`, there is no mapping to exclude against, so every absolute mount target is reported as container-only — including a bind that in fact covers the workspace. It is a prompt fact, not a guard, and erring toward "the host may not see this" is the safe direction; the alternative (guessing the CLI's default workspace target) would fabricate a fact.

RECORDED (pre-existing). A still-listed but stopped candidate passes the new membership test while `selectionFor` stamps the entry's state, so `bind()` can report `selected-valid` for a stopped container; the adapter then hands the CLI `--container-id <stopped>` and the CLI fails. There is no wrong-container risk (the id is real), and the failure is typed; a future pass could cross-check the candidate's state instead.

LIMITATION, RESTATED. Three behaviours now live in the extension's command dispatch, which this repository has no unit harness for: delivering a handler's rendered result, draining the discovery diagnostics, and the new engagement gate. Their policy halves are unit-tested (`displayCommandResult`, `reportDiscoveryDiagnostics`, `allowsAutoSelection`) and the wiring rests on the packed smoke run; a change to the dispatch must be smoke-checked rather than trusted to the unit suite.
